llama.e:
Etymology tree
Quechua llamabor.
Spanish llamabor.
English llama
Borrowed from Spanish llama, borrowed from Quechua llama.

s.d: wild or domesticated South American cud-chewing animal related to camels but smaller and lacking a hump
A South American mammal of the camel family, Lama glama, used as a domestic beast of burden and a source of wool and meat.

llano.e: Borrowed from Spanish llano. Doublet of piano, plain, plane, and plan.

s.d: an extensive grassy and nearly treeless plain (especially in Latin America)
A plain or steppe in parts of Latin America.
x: “For this,” said El Espinero, with an economical slide of his hand indicating all the visible circumference of the cruel llano.
